pairs.why: A's jellyfish has softer, glowing translucent edges and fewer sharp internal contours, closer to the real jellyfish's soft rim-lit silhouette, though B's frills are only slightly crisper.
B's calculator has a slightly softer outer edge, while A's keys have crisper separations and a heavier dark body, but the glow halo in B is a counterweight so the difference is small.
Both corals have similar soft clay edges, bumpy dotted texture edges and the same rock contours, so edges give no reason to choose.
A's duck has slightly softer, rounder edges, while B has crisper thin handle edges and more edge noise in the sand; the real duck has smooth soft rim edges.
A's rim and hands are softer-edged and the hour hand is fatter and tapered like the real clock's, while B has thinner crisp lines and a hard ground-shadow line.
A's stone chess table has softer, broader edges and fewer tiny checker edges, closer to the real table's chunky, smooth contours, while B's smaller checker squares add busy fine edges.
A's clock hands and ticks are chunkier with a softer rim, matching the real clock's thick tapered shapes, while B has thin hairline hands and a hard floor shadow edge.
B's coral has softer edges and a darker, lost-edge rock base, while A's bright rocks show sharper facets and a higher edge density; the real card has soft, lost edges.
